title: Lift four P104 helper inputs: conditional κ 0.003129111
body:
Four existing helper inputs now start at native subspaces of dimensions 1, 1, 1 and 3. Explicit correlated input directions and output basis corrections preserve all 770 independent inputs. The complete conditional claim improves from PR6167's **κ = 0.003128645** to **κ = 0.003129111**, a gain of **0.000000466 (0.0149%)**. This is a small gain; no large breakthrough is claimed.

The direct source is DreamingOfClouds' PR6314, head `36533d4d1b4e2dd8672427461b12de3001b85810`, which compresses PR6167 without changing its recursive price. The new word has 17,452 events. Its local paid change is `H1 + H2 + H3 + 2H4 - 4H5`; its productive target debit is `H6 + 3H8 - 4H9`. The complete p16/a7 caller has 66,780 paid calls, 13,444 targets and rank surplus 760. Every query, helper normalizer, adapter, owned operation, route, completion and compiler cost remains charged.

The strict raw crossing is `(0.00312911821812, 0.00312911821813)`. The old complete profile fails at the new claimed κ. The general concave-tariff comparison is inconclusive; the claim uses the exact power-moment checks at the stated exponent.

- [Proof and complete dependency argument](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/af7cb6c67f8fc7d82a2e4aee2dd2f07481bf6690/research/p104-native-input-lifting/PROOF.md)
- [Exact result and rejection controls](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/af7cb6c67f8fc7d82a2e4aee2dd2f07481bf6690/research/p104-native-input-lifting/RESULT.json)
- [Source pins and reproducible package](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/tree/af7cb6c67f8fc7d82a2e4aee2dd2f07481bf6690/research/p104-native-input-lifting)
- [Canonical claim and overlap record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5645#discussioncomment-19205459)

Validation on CPython 3.12.13, macOS 26.6.1 arm64: the direct normal verifier and both registered normal/optimized replays pass. They check all 799 columns and 638,401 endpoint coefficients, a separate dense transpose, 2,930 native maps with exact phases, the full physical caller, two rational moment engines, completion/compiler bounds, and 54 strict plus four functional outer predicates. All declared semantic and source-corruption controls reject. Metadata, live pins, committed bytes/modes and the official 18-file export pass. The full normal and optimized replays also pass from a read-only export with empty PATH and no Git. All 19 files (18 payload files plus the export receipt) and all 25 file/directory paths retain their bytes and modes. Export SHA256: `445f9b9330dc01ec516d41d179ad4a9a22f501c2ec457b2e25aff79bc9bb3137`. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41372638075) passes both the planner and the full registered package replay, including the committed-input check.

Publication head `af7cb6c67f8fc7d82a2e4aee2dd2f07481bf6690` is a direct child of canonical main `626e936ce4d61f2584316914fc71baf96940c512`, priority revision 8. All declared source pins resolve at that base. Full-history preflight mode was not run in this shallow checkout. The five inherited framework assumptions remain: `native_all_columns`, `owned_erasure`, `compiler`, `precision_tape`, and `analytic_recovery`. The uniform word and rounded multiplier are not materialized. Author checks are not independent scientific acceptance. The selected frontier and protected contact blocks are unchanged.

This input-boundary mechanism is separate from Discussion5600's fixed-boundary public-prefix rewrite and [PR6348's tree caller](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6348). It provides a complete local supplier for later composition, with its changed target profile explicitly recorded; no composition with the new tree caller is claimed here.

New work: Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents. PR6314 retains DreamingOfClouds and Claude Opus 5.5 credit. The unchanged source/checker chain retains Cinna Davis, David Arias, Gareth Davidson, Jacob Alan Sussman, zxv, Cao Yifan, flyingviper, Pierre-Loic Doulcet, Joel Pulikkan, Scratch-net and all earlier source authors in NOTICE.
